Triage (objectstack triage seat, R+149, 2026-09-04T18:13Z): lands in `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx` ⇒ `domain:ui`. Graded `Bug` · `priority:p3`.

⚠️ This card sat **6 days** untriaged — objectui's first-touch queue has been structurally starved behind objectstack's older cards under oldest-first ordering. Measured and now in the maintainer's inbox as objectstack#15476. ⛔ Not the filer's problem.

`Bug`: `??` replaces only `null` / `undefined`, so a degenerate `properties` passes into the object spread and is re-read as its own character indices. Identical hazard to the five #6783 converged, on the same channel, in a **different expression** — `{ ...schema, ...schema.properties }` rather than `{ ...schema.props, ...schema.properties }`, so no `props` alias leg but the node's own keys underneath.

### `priority:p3`, and the card bounds it honestly

⛔ **Not a live failure.** #6708's census walked every JSON document, every `json` doc fence and every TypeScript object literal and found **zero** authored nodes carrying a degenerate config bag. And `record-alert` reads only **named** keys off the bag (`props.title`, `props.body`, `props.severity`, `props.action?.label`, `props.dismissible`, …) and never spreads it onto a DOM element ⇒ **the indexed keys are computed and then dropped; nothing rendered moves either way.**

⭐ What the guard buys is what #6752 measured for its own: **the authored value's shape is not reinterpreted.** That is worth doing and it is not urgent.

⚠️ It is also **known ground, not a new discovery** — `alias-precedence-cross-channel.test.tsx`'s docblock already names this site as the sixth member. What is new is that #6783 converged the other five and left this one alone, so it is now the **only** member out of step.

### Two things to establish before writing code

⚠️ **The dependency edge.** After #6783 the guard is a one-line import — `isConfigBag` is exported from `@object-ui/react`'s package entry — ⛔ but `@object-ui/plugin-detail` has to be **checked** for that edge. `@object-ui/components` already had it, which is what made #6783's fix a read rather than a sixth spelling. ⇒ If the edge is absent, adding it is a separate call, not a rider.

⚠️ **⛔ Do not reuse the shared reader without deciding where it lives.** #6783's `readProps` sits at `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/readProps.ts` and is **not exported** from `@object-ui/components` (its barrel is side-effect imports only). ⇒ Reusing the *reader* rather than just the *predicate* is a separate decision about where it belongs. Taking the predicate alone keeps this card small.

⭐ The alternative arm is legitimate and should be answered rather than skipped: **rule that this reader may reinterpret whatever it is handed, and say so at the reader.** If the lane takes that, the deliverable is the sentence, not the guard.

### ⛔ Four sites already checked and deliberately NOT part of this

The card pre-empted the next sweep, and that work should not be redone: `record-activity.tsx:105` and `ResourceEditPage.tsx:1285` are **keyed reads with no spread** (a degenerate value yields `undefined` per key); the remaining `metadata-admin` hits (`SchemaForm.tsx`, `widgets.tsx`, `mergeServerFields.ts`, `json-schema-to-fields.ts`, `datasource/DatasourceResourcePage.tsx`, `previews/ToolPreview.tsx`) read a **JSON Schema** `properties` map, ⛔ not the SDUI config bag.

⚠️ Measured on `107babef6` (2026-08-29). Locate `readProps` by symbol and re-confirm the line still spreads before editing.

## PM contract review — arm 1 taken, PR #8639 accepted, flipped out of draft, auto-merge armed

### ⭐ The arm was chosen on merits, and the decisive point is one neither triage nor I had

The order said explicitly not to default to the guard because it is the larger diff. The justification given is better than "it's small":

> **Arm 2 is not smaller in files touched** — `alias-precedence-cross-channel.test.tsx`'s docblock names this site as a same-order family member and would need amending too.

⇒ The "cheaper" arm was **not actually cheaper**. Plus: the dependency edge already existed, so triage's "if the edge is absent, that is a separate call" branch never applied; and arm 2 would have been *"a per-site exception resting on an accident of current usage — named reads, no onward spread — that is **one spread away from false** and would need its own pin to stay true."*

That last point is the real argument. An exception justified by how the code happens to read its bag today is a liability the moment someone adds a spread.

### The discriminating input was placed where it can actually discriminate

> The pin reads **the bag, not the DOM**, because the renderer drops the indices, so a render-level pin cannot see the defect **on either implementation**.

That is the p3 reasoning turned into test design: the card says nothing rendered moves, so a DOM assertion is structurally incapable of separating the two. `BASE_READING` from the revert leg is quoted verbatim — indexed keys `['0'..'8']` for the string, `['0','1']` for the array.

⭐ And there is a pin for **what the guard does not buy** — *"a degenerate bag renders exactly as no bag at all"* — recorded as **green pre-fix too**. Pinning the non-consequence, and labelling it a characterization rather than evidence, is the honest way to hold a p3's own claim.

### The four legs, and why L4 matters most

L1 (revert) 3 red · L2 (predicate constant-false) 2 red · L3 (reader returns a constant) 5 red · **L4 (inline retelling with `Array.isArray`) — 1 red, the structural pin only.**

L4 is an implementation that behaves correctly and still violates the requirement: re-spelling the predicate instead of importing it. Only the structural pin catches it — which is precisely what a structural pin is for, and it is now demonstrated rather than assumed.

### Two pieces of discipline worth naming

1. ⭐ **The module move was forced, not stylistic, and the baseline was measured first.** Exporting the reader from `record-alert.tsx` tripped a **new** `react-refresh/only-export-components` warning against a **baseline of 0 on that file**, so the reader moved to its own module (mirroring #6783's layout). `index.tsx` imports `RecordAlertRenderer` by name, so nothing new reaches the package entry.
2. ⭐ **The verification harness was audited by content, not trusted.** The final locked run chained ablation and vitest with `;`, so the lock's `VERDICT` line is batch-last-exit — that was **noticed and disclosed**, with each part's exit captured separately and the verdicts read from content. Applying "verify by content, never by exit code" to the verifier itself is the right instinct.

And **the type-check trap the order named fired for real**: an early draft of the pin file was **vitest-green but tsc-red** (TS2353/TS2559 on off-type render inputs), caught before push. That is the third measurement today of the same class — vitest and `tsc` disagreeing on a test file — and it keeps earning its place in dispatches.

`check:phantom-deps` verdict quoted (*"Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it"*), no edge added, predicate-only per triage, and the four already-checked sites correctly left alone.
